newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore trade skeptical about Thai rubber buying.
newsitem.headline: Singapore trade skeptical about Thai rubber buying.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market reacted on Wednesday with skepticism to the plan by the Thai government to buy more RSS3 grade rubber, dealers said.
An official of the Thai agriculture ministry claimed rubber demand remained strong and that Bangkok hopes to clinch deals with China and the EU.
"But there are really no buyers for the rubber. Who are they going to sell the rubber to? How long can they sustain this subsidy?" one dealer for a North American trading house said.
Trading in the local market remained dull, dealers said. "People are winding down for the Easter holidays," one said.
"The buyers are saying offer me a price and then they sit it out," one trader said. "There's not much happenning today."
"People are very cautious now ahead of the holidays. People are squaring their positions before the expiry" of the April RSS3 contract this month, a dealer added.
Another trader said the April contract may be squeezed on the downside at the approach of the expiry.
At around 0945 GMT, May RSS3 was seen at 121.00 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 121.50 cents. October/December TSR20 was seen at 117.00-119.00 U.S. cents a kg from 119.25 cents.
